newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: First petrol ship since coup arrives in Freetown.
newsitem.headline: First petrol ship since coup arrives in Freetown.

text.p: The first shipment of petrol to reach Sierra Leone since the military coup on May 25 arrived at Freetown docks on Sunday night, officials said on Monday.
Shipping agents said the Hong Kong-registered Jian She 31 carried 55,000 tonnes of petrol and 2,000 tonnes of gas oil.
"The head of state went to inspect the petrol and talk to the crew," government spokesman Allieu Kamara said.
Junta leader Johnny Paul Koroma is under pressure from neighbouring West African states to restore ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

Diplomatic talks broke down at the end of July when Koroma said the junta would be staying in power for four years, and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) said it would step up sanctions against the regime, backed by a sea, land and air blockade.
It was unclear how the ship, which the agents said had come from Dakar, Senegal, had managed to get through the blockade.

A shipment of rice and a ship carrying oil for power generators have also got through recently. The latter did not lead to the city's lights being switched back on, since the generators still have no lubricants or cooling agents.
The junta is continuing to make diplomatic efforts to resolve the impasse.
Government spokesman Kamara said a mission went to Guinea on Saturday to meet Guinean President Lansana Conte.
It wanted to secure his recognition of the military regime and ask him not to allow Guinean troops, in Sierra Leone with the ECOWAS mission, get involved in fighting.

Kamara said Conte had agreed to visit Sierra Leone before a planned ECOWAS summit on August 27-29, but West African diplomats doubted that he would come, given the blanket condemnation of the junta by international bodies including the United Nations.
